title: Learned network features relate to simulated protein-network mechanics
summary: Gradient-boosted surrogates linked imaged network geometry to simulated mechanical responses. Density features dominated stress/strain estimates; segment inhomogeneity was most important for simulated buckling. These are conditional computational relationships, not measured in-vivo mechanics.
organization: University of Stuttgart; University of Freiburg

evidence.tested: Thirty-seven imaged networks supported finite-element simulations; surrogate training/test contained33/4 networks with fivefold training cross-validation.
evidence.unknown: Linear elasticity, generic loading and failure criteria borrowed from another filament system limit interpretation. Imaging resolution and the four-network test restrict confidence. No causal architecture or experimentally measured mechanical function is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Learned surrogates map26 structural descriptors to simulated responses and rank feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Computational Methods2.5–2.7, Results3.4 and limitations4.4; primary front/date/status. Experimental preparation sections were not used.
